instruction_spec.task_title: Build product-summary slides from inventory JSON using template deck
instruction_spec.information_flow: linux.json (first Linux) -> filter/transform approved products -> linux.odp_pptx template (second Linux) -> create updated ODP deck on second Linux
instruction_spec.instruction: On the first Linux device, open the product inventory JSON at /home/user/data/products.json. On the second Linux device, open the presentation template /home/user/presentations/template.odp and create a new presentation named /home/user/presentations/product_updates.odp. For every product in the JSON whose status is "approved", add a Product Summary slide (one per approved product) using the template slide and fill the text anchors so each slide shows Product ID, Name, Version, and Status. Save the deck at the target path on the second Linux device.
instruction_spec.detailed_description: Read the JSON inventory on the first Linux device. The JSON contains a list of product records (product_id, name, version, status). Select only records where status == "approved". On the second Linux device there is an ODP template deck containing a template slide titled "Template Slide: Product Summary" with text anchors for PRODUCT_ID, PRODUCT_NAME, VERSION, STATUS. For each approved product, create a new slide based on that template slide and populate the anchors with the product's product_id, name, version, and status. Save the resulting ODP deck as /home/user/presentations/product_updates.odp. The required output semantics: the saved deck must contain one Product Summary slide per approved product from the JSON and each such slide must include deterministic text anchors with the Product ID, Name, Version and Status values taken from the JSON. The expected_data values (product IDs, names, versions, statuses) are directly taken from the JSON source; the mapping to slides is determined by the presence of the template slide anchors in the template ODP on the second device.
instruction_spec.why_cross_device: The product records (the authoritative data) are on the first Linux device as a JSON file, while the slide template and the final presentation must be created/updated on the second Linux device; creating per-product slides therefore requires reading data on the first device and writing the updated deck on the second device.

asset_manifest.content: A JSON array of product records. Must include at least three products and contain the approved anchors P-200 (SpectraCam 2.1, approved) and P-305 (AeroNav 1.4, approved).
asset_manifest.format_notes: Write a UTF-8 JSON array file at /home/user/data/products.json. Each entry is an object with keys product_id, name, version, status. Include several distractor and non-approved records so the agent must filter by status == "approved".

asset_manifest.content: An ODP template deck JSON spec containing 5 slides including a template slide titled "Template Slide: Product Summary" with text anchors PRODUCT_ID, PRODUCT_NAME, VERSION, STATUS. The template slide should include placeholder tokens {PRODUCT_ID}, {PRODUCT_NAME}, {VERSION}, {STATUS} so automation can replace them.
asset_manifest.format_notes: Generate an ODP at /home/user/presentations/template.odp according to the JSON spec provided in external_files. The deck must have 5 slides with titles: Title, Agenda, Template Slide: Product Summary, Contact, Credits. The Product Summary slide must include plain-text anchor tokens exactly PRODUCT_ID, PRODUCT_NAME, VERSION, STATUS (or placeholders {PRODUCT_ID} etc.) so a script can locate and replace them.

elements.text: Use this slide to summarize approved product changes.

hidden_oracle.name: approved_products_list
hidden_oracle.content: From products.json the approved records are P-200 (SpectraCam, 2.1, approved), P-305 (AeroNav, 1.4, approved), and P-420 (DockLight, 3.2, approved). The Stage1 expected_data and value_trace require slides for P-200 and P-305 specifically; evaluator will check for at least the two specified approved anchors P-200 and P-305. Total approved_count in the provided file: 3.

setup_visibility_checks: On linux_0: /home/user/data/products.json exists and is readable; it contains the visible anchors P-200 and P-305 required by the task.
On linux_1: /home/user/presentations/template.odp exists and contains the template slide titled "Template Slide: Product Summary" with text anchors PRODUCT_ID, PRODUCT_NAME, VERSION, STATUS.
On linux_1: /home/user/presentations/product_updates.odp does not exist before agent execution (ensures a clean target for the updated deck).

result.command: count=$(unzip -p /home/user/presentations/product_updates.odp content.xml 2>/dev/null | grep -c '<draw:page'); if [ -z "$count" ]; then echo slides_low; elif [ "$count" -ge 2 ]; then echo slides_ok; else echo slides_low; fi

metadata.notes: Score-enabled checks validate (1) ODP text anchors populated for both approved products and presence of 'Product Updates' in the presentation, and (2) slide count >= 2. Input JSON content is sanity-checked as a non-scoring guard.

scripted_solution_plan: On linux_1, create the final ODP /home/user/presentations/product_updates.odp containing the presentation title with the phrase 'Product Updates', include one Product Summary slide per approved product (P-200 and P-305) and ensure the text anchors in each slide are populated with the corresponding PRODUCT_ID/PRODUCT_NAME/VERSION/STATUS strings.

For the negative oracle, create an ODP that omits one of the required product anchors (so a score-enabled text check will fail) while leaving slide count >= 2 to isolate the failure to the text anchors check.

positive_oracle_steps.notes: Creates an ODP with >=2 draw:page entries and text content including all required anchors and a document title that contains 'Product Updates'.

negative_oracle_steps.title: Product Updates - Partial
negative_oracle_steps.notes: Deliberately omits the P-305 / AeroNav anchors so the check_odf_text evaluator (which requires both products) will fail while slide count remains >=2.
